• **Magnification formula:** The magnification (*m*) of a spherical mirror is mathematically represented as **m = -v/u**, where:

 
 
• **v**: Image distance (distance from the mirror to the image).
 
• **u**: Object distance (distance from the mirror to the object).
 
 
 
• **Understanding the magnification:**

• A magnification value (**|m|**) less than 1 indicates a diminished (smaller) image. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Spherical mirrors:**

 
 
• **Concave mirror:** A spherical mirror whose reflecting surface is curved inward.

 
 
• Forms real and inverted images if the object is placed beyond the focal point.
 
• Forms virtual and erect images when the object is placed between the focal point and the mirror.
 
 
 
• **Convex mirror:** A spherical mirror whose reflecting surface is curved outward.
 
 
• Always forms virtual, erect, and diminished images irrespective of the object’s position.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Magnification types:**
 
 
• **Positive magnification:** Indicates a virtual and erect image.
 
• **Negative magnification:** Indicates a real and inverted image.
 
 
 
• **Applications of concave and convex mirrors:**
 
 
• **Concave mirrors:** Used in headlights, shaving mirrors, and reflecting telescopes due to their ability to converge light.
 
• **Convex mirrors:** Used in vehicle rear-view mirrors and security mirrors as they provide a wider field of view.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Sign conventions for mirrors:**

 
 
• Distances measured in the direction of incident light are positive, and those measured against it are negative.
 
• Height of objects and images is positive if measured upward and negative if measured downward.
 
 
 
• **Important formulas:**
 
 
• **Mirror equation:** 1/f = 1/v + 1/u
 
• **Magnification:** m = -v/u
